'''Chikugo River Fireworks Festival''' (筑後川花火大会) is a [[Fireworks Festival|Fireworks]] held every August in [[Kurume|Kurume City]], [[Fukuoka Prefecture]].
== Overview ==
It attracts over 450,000 spectators every year, and the riverside of the [[Chikugo River]] – the largest river in [[Kyushu]] – serves as the venue.
Approximately 18,000 [[Fireworks]] are launched annually, making it one of the largest in [[Western Japan]], and it is the only major fireworks festival held solely in Fukuoka Prefecture with over 10,000 launches (the [[Kanmon Straits Fireworks Festival]], with about 15,000 launches, is co-hosted with Yamaguchi Prefecture). Excellent star mines with a well-structured ([[Kishōtenketsu|Kishotenten]]) design, large-scale mechanized fireworks including the Niagara, and giant shell fireworks burst forth like enormous blossoms in the night sky. The event is bustling with many couples and families dressed in [[Yukata]], while over 400 [[Market stall|Stall]] line the venue, and vendors offering Kurume [[B-class Gourmet|B-class gourmet]] also participate. The Chikugo River Fireworks Festival is an [[Event|event]] presented as the dedicated fireworks for the Suitengu Summer Festival, and historically it is unrelated to the "Kurume Water Festival."
== History ==
It originated in [[1650]] (the 3rd year of [[Keian]]) when the lord of the [[Kurume Domain]], [[Arima Tadayori]], donated a shrine building to the [[Kurume Suitengū|Suitengu]] site and dedicated fireworks to celebrate its completion. Subsequently, it was held as the "Suitengu Dedication Fireworks Festival" and, after nine cancellations due to turmoil and wars, adopted its current name in [[1965]] (the 40th year of [[Shōwa era|Showa]]).
Furthermore, with the integration of various city festivals into the Kurume Water Festival starting in [[1972]] (Showa 47), the event also came to signify the finale of that festival.
Originally held solely on the riverside in front of Suitengu, following the [[Akashi pedestrian bridge accident|Akashi Fireworks Pedestrian Bridge Accident]] in [[2001]] (the 13th year of [[Heisei era|Heisei]]), from [[2004]] (Heisei 16) the then-[[Kurume Police Station]] [[Police Chief|Chief]] initiated a split launch with the Shino-yama Venue located on the Kurume Castle riverside. Accordingly, the original venue was renamed "Kyomachi Venue." Furthermore, from [[2005]] (Heisei 17), [[Tosu, Saga|Tosu City]] joined as a co-host, establishing a viewing area at the sports field in Shimonochō on the border of Kurume City as the "Tosu Venue."
In [[2019]] (the first year of Reiwa), the Kurume City Violence Expulsion Promotion Council intensified efforts to exclude [[Yakuza|Japanese organized crime group]] from the [[Market stall|Stall]] vendors participating in the festival, instituting a rule that all stalls must display the "Violence Expulsion Declaration Plate" distributed by the city.
In [[2020]] (Reiwa 2) and the following [[2021]] (Reiwa 3), the event was cancelled due to the [[COVID-19 Outbreak in Japan|COVID-19 Outbreak]].
In [[2022]] (Reiwa 4), the festival was held for the first time in three years; however, due to movement restrictions during the COVID-19 outbreak, the number of launches was reduced to approximately 8,000 and the launch duration to 30 minutes, significantly downsizing the event.<ref>[http://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1500soshiki/9119kanko/3010oshirase/2022-0707-1856-289.html ]</ref> Additionally, during the event, an accident occurred in which a firework shell fell and exploded at the archery field of the [[Kurume National College of Technology]], located approximately 260 meters from the launch site.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|和書|title=弓道場に花火玉が落下した事故、製造や打ち上げ時のミスが原因か…調査報告書 |url=https://www.yomiuri.co.jp/national/20221121-OYT1T50251/ |website=読売新聞オンライン |date=2022-11-21 |access-date=2022-11-21 |language=ja|qq=}}</ref> The accident was attributed to a combination of human errors and other factors.<ref name=":0" />
In [[2023]] (Reiwa 5), the event date was changed to August 27, and if inclement weather prevents the event from taking place on that day, it will be cancelled rather than postponed. The Tosu Venue was not set up, the number of launches was set at 15,000, and the launch duration at 70 minutes (with the end time advanced to 20:50), marking a reduction in scale compared to prior to [[2019]].<ref>{{Cite web|和書|url=https://www.nishinippon.co.jp/item/n/1102583/ |title=筑後川花火大会、今年は8月27日開催　福岡・久留米市、1万5千発規模に |access-date=2023-06-30 |publisher=西日本新聞me|qq=}}</ref>
== Date and Time ==
: It is held on [[August 5]] every year regardless of the day of the week. In case of rain, it is postponed on alternate days to [[August 7|7th]], [[August 9|9th]], and [[August 11|11th]].
: Typically, fireworks are launched from 19:40 to 21:10.
※ Until 2019
== Venue ==
Six venues are provided as fireworks viewing locations. At the Shino-yama Venue, shell fireworks begin to be launched around 20:15. Since the riverside of the [[Chikugo River]] is spacious, it is possible to walk between venues (the Kyomachi Venue and the Shino-yama Venue).
In suburban areas without obstacles such as buildings, one can watch the fireworks standing; however, the overwhelming impact as experienced at the venue is diminished.
=== Viewing Locations ===
All venues are located on the riverside of the [[Chikugo River]], and unless otherwise noted, are situated in [[Kurume|Kurume City]], [[Fukuoka Prefecture]].
* Kyomachi Venue – Riverside on the left bank in front of Suitengu from Nisenmanbashi to [[Nagatoishi Bridge]]
** Nagatoishi Venue – Right bank riverside around [[Nagatoishi Bridge]]
** Miyaki Venue ([[Saga Prefecture]][[Miyaki, Saga|Miyaki Town]]) – Right bank riverside upstream of [[Mamezu Bridge]]
* Shino-yama Venue – Riverside on the left bank in front of Kurume Castle from [[Nagatoishi Bridge]] to [[Mamezu Bridge]]
** Komorino Venue – Right bank riverside from [[Komorino Bridge]] to Nisenmanbashi
** Tosu Venue ([[Saga Prefecture]][[Tosu, Saga|Tosu City]]) – Right bank at Shimonochō Sports Field ※ Not set up in [[2023]]
=== Launch Locations ===
* Across from Kyomachi Venue
* Across from Shino-yama Venue
== Traffic Restrictions ==
Vehicular traffic is prohibited primarily on the embankment road between [[Kurume Ohashi]] and [[Mamezu Bridge]], as well as along both banks of the [[Chikugo River]]. In all cases, restrictions are enforced from 18:30 to 22:00 (with some sections until 22:30).
; No Entry
* Embankment road along the right bank of the Chikugo River behind [[Kurume National College of Technology]] and along the left bank of the [[Homan River|Hōman River]] (launch location for Shino-yama Venue)
* A section of the embankment road along the right bank of the Chikugo River between [[Nagatoishi Bridge]] and [[Mamezu Bridge]] (launch location for Kyomachi Venue)
* [[Komorino Bridge]]
* Downstream sidewalk of [[Nagatoishi Bridge]]
; Road Closed to Vehicles
* All roads on the left bank riverside of the [[Chikugo River]] from the [[Mamezu Bridge]] Intersection – Suitengu Entrance Intersection – Nawa-te Intersection – Keyaki Street – Kushihara Bypass – East Intersection of the Fire Department Headquarters – from the south end of Nisenmanbashi
** [[Fukuoka Prefecture Road 145 Eguchi Nagatoishi Eshima Line|Saga Prefectural Road and Fukuoka Prefectural Road Route 145]] and [[Nagatoishi Bridge]] are exempt from restrictions
** From Asahimachi Intersection on I-Dai Street to in front of the University Hospital serves as a shuttle bus waiting area
* Embankment road on both banks between [[Kurume Ohashi]] and [[Komorino Bridge]]
* Embankment road along the right bank of the Anra River, [[Homan River|Hōman River]], and the Chikugo River from [[Torinan Bridge]] to [[Mamezu Bridge]]
* Embankment road on the west side of [[Fukuoka/Saga Prefecture Road 17 Kurume Motoyama Chikushino Line|Fukuoka Prefectural Road and Saga Prefectural Road Route 17]]
* Road from Shimonochō Intersection to the riverside of the Chikugo River
* Road from the intersection in front of [[Hizen-Asahi Station|Hizen Asahi Station]] to the riverside of the Chikugo River
== Access ==
=== Rail and Bus ===
* Kyomachi Venue – Walk from [[Kyushu Railway Company|JR]] [[Kurume Station]]
* Shino-yama Venue – Take a temporary bus from [[Nishitetsu Kurume Station]] and alight at the University Hospital bus stop ([[Kurume University Hospital]])
* Komorino Venue – 20-minute walk from [[Miyanojin Station]]
* Tosu Venue – 30-minute walk from [[Hizen-Asahi Station|Hizen Asahi Station]]
* Nagatoishi Venue – Alight at the Welfare Center bus stop on Nishitetsu Bus route 40
* Miyaki Venue – Alight at the Mamezu Bus Stop on Nishitetsu Bus routes 41 or 45
On the day of the event, temporary trains will operate on JR and Nishitetsu lines. The shuttle bus runs only between [[Nishitetsu Kurume Station]] and the University Hospital bus stop near Shino-yama Venue ([[Kurume University Hospital]]). As all venues are within approximately 2 km of Kurume Station, walking between them is also feasible.
=== Private Car ===
Due to traffic restrictions and congestion on the day of the event, it is difficult to enter central Kurume City by private car, and no parking is provided; therefore, the use of public transportation is strongly encouraged (in the past, the parking lot of [[Ekimae Real Estate Stadium|Front Station Real Estate Stadium]], adjacent to [[Tosu Station]], was opened on the day of the event, but this has now been discontinued).
